source.title: Neuroscience-Inspired Analyses of Visual Interestingness in Multimodal Transformers
source.authors: Mathis Immertreu; Fitim Abdullahu; T. Kinfe; Helmut Grabner; Patrick Krauss; Achim Schilling

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Figure graphics are not available in the text, so plotted values that are not described in prose cannot be extracted.
record.tranche_reason: Conceptual test of whether an SAE can recover a feature-related direction, using SAE-based probing in a multimodal transformer rather than the original toy-model superposition method.
record.gate_note: The paper cites Toy Models of Superposition as background and mentions features existing in superposition, but it does not test superposition, capacity competition, feature sparsity or importance, polysemanticity, or whether features are one-dimensional versus multidimensional. Its relevant result is an SAE-based extraction of a CI-related direction in Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct. Other representation analyses, including the reported linear-readout and GDV results, do not directly test SAE feature recovery.
record.test_reason: The study uses an SAE as one of six ways to build a CI concept vector in Qwen3-VL-8B. It reports only how well each method's projection correlates with CI scores. The SAE vector is a supervised, correlation-weighted sum of 32 atoms, not a test of whether the model holds sparse features a dictionary recovers. It does not measure feature overlap, polysemanticity, capacity, SAE completeness or stability, or feature dimensionality. Toy Models of Superposition is cited only as background.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude CI is linearly decodable from final-layer embeddings (regression r = 0.776, R² = 0.575). CI structure strengthens from vision to deeper LLM layers by GDV. Geometric, probe and SAE-based concept vectors converge in deeper layers. RSA shows CI remains a distributed property rather than an isolated feature. They flag the coarse partition-level CI and shared CLIP/SigLIP priors as limitations.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes CI representations in a pretrained multimodal transformer using regression, layerwise geometry, concept-vector extraction, and SAE-based dictionary learning; it does not reproduce the original toy-model method.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported CI structure varies across model layers and extraction methods; the paper describes stronger alignment in deeper LLM layers than in early vision layers and greater variability for some geometric methods.

fits_no_version.finding: A CI direction built from 16 positively and 16 negatively CI-correlated SAE atoms correlates with partition-level interestingness scores. Text reports methods converge in LLM L31–36 at r = 0.6–0.7, with SAE among the most consistent.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Human-derived visual interestingness is linearly decodable from multimodal transformer representations, including via supervised combinations of SAE atoms.

record.problems: The evidence concerns one model checkpoint and a coarse partition-level CI measure. The authors note shared representational priors between CLIP-based CI construction and the SigLIP-2-initialized vision encoder. No causal intervention establishes the functional role of the recovered direction, and no SAE-specific numerical correlation is stated outside the figure.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows for the paper’s regression-head or GDV results: these analyze CI information in representations but do not directly measure SAE feature recovery. The paper’s plotted method-level results do not provide extractable SAE-specific values.

untested.parts: No toy models, sparsity sweeps or feature geometry.
No test of capacity competition. The Discussion's remark that PCA (1st) lags because capacity goes to other demands is interpretation, not a test.
No neuron-level distribution analysis. No evaluation of SAE reconstruction, sparsity or feature interpretability. The SAE is only a tool for building a CI direction.
No test of SAE feature completeness, stability or canonicity.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T2' and V4 'supports' are overturned. Using an SAE as an extraction tool and reporting only its correlation with a target is a T4 use, not evidence about superposition or dictionary recovery.

versions.untested_parts: Toy networks, feature-to-dimension ratios, overlap geometry, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry.
Whether capacity competition causes polysemanticity or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
Alternative causes of polysemanticity and whether polysemanticity occurs without capacity pressure.
The study tests SAE-based recovery of a CI-related direction in one multimodal model; it does not establish generality across LLMs or test features spread across neurons by neuron-level analysis.
Completeness, stability, or canonical status of SAE features.
Whether the features involved in superposition are one-dimensional rather than multidimensional.

rows.subject: Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Extracted CI concept vectors using sparse dictionary learning: an SAE with 49,152 overcomplete features and top-K activation 16; formed the vector from correlation-weighted SAE atoms.
rows.measure: Pearson correlation between concept-vector projection values and CI scores
rows.value: figure only; text says sparse dictionary learning showed consistent performance and that methods converged at LLM L31–36 with r = 0.6–0.7 overall; no SAE-specific coefficient is stated
rows.locator: Results, “Interestingness forms a linear concept direction”; Fig. 6b
rows.note: The plot does not provide extractable layer-specific SAE values in the supplied text. The prose attributes the broad convergence result to the methods collectively and describes sparse dictionary learning as among the most consistent; it does not isolate an SAE-specific coefficient.
rows.check: The row reports method performance for a supervised readout built from SAE atoms (32 atoms, correlation-weighted), compared against other extraction methods. It measures CI decodability, not whether sparse dictionary features exist or are recovered, so it does not bear on V4. No SAE-specific coefficient is stated in the text (figure only). The 'observed' state against V4 is unfounded.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
